newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S., China begin arms talks in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: U.S., China begin arms talks in Beijing.

text.p: A senior U.S. official began talks on Wednesday with his Chinese counterparts on nuclear technology and arms control issues, an U.S. embassy official said.
Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Robert Einhorn is leading the United States side during three days of talks that also cover chemical weapons and missile technology.
"These talks are a continuation of discussions that the two sides have held over the past year," an embassy official told Reuters.
A key issue will be how the United States might put into effect a 1985 agreement with China on cooperation in the peaceful use of nuclear technology.
Implementation of the accord would allow major U.S. companies to export nuclear technology to China where there is huge demand for energy, including nuclear power.

But U.S. exports have been stalled by Washington's suspicions that Beijing was exporting nuclear technology to unsafeguarded nuclear facilities abroad, most notably Pakistan. China and Pakistan have denied the allegations.
China agreed last May not to provide nuclear technology to unsafeguarded facilities, and U.S. officials have said they were looking forward to an early implementation of the Sino-U.S. pact.

Efforts to resolve remaining differences gained momentum during a visit last year by then U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher when the two sides agreed to meet regularly to discuss non-proliferation and arms control issues.
